notes: Initial idea from user on 2026-05-07: add MCP scopes as query or path parameters that shape the exposed MCP tool set. Daystrom sibling repo has a simple precedent: /mcp?scope={main|ops|all} resolves a per-session tool catalog by tagging ops-only tools with DaystromOpsScopeAttribute and installing a scoped ToolCollection in ConfigureSessionOptions. In blackbox, existing primitives are global/project/brofile/per-dispatch McpFilters with allow/disallow glob patterns plus provider-specific translation. Candidate direction: add named scope/filter packets that compose into McpFilters at MCP-session/list-tools time and/or dispatch-time, complementing existing allow/disallow rather than replacing them. Key design question: whether scopes are only visibility views for this daemon's own MCP endpoint, reusable dispatch filter packets for bros, or one unified named rule-packet layer used by both.

Deeper scout correction after user pushback: blackbox already has a generic inlet routing architecture that should shape MCP surfaces if possible. Current pattern: raw inlet payload + headers -> workflow::extractor::Extractor flat entity -> rule-packet classification -> routing::resolve_entity_template -> typed RoutingVerdict -> dispatch_routed_event / dispatch_routing_verdict_direct. Webhooks, pollers, crons, and whiteboard transitions converge here. Existing RoutingVerdict variants are start_arc, signal_arc, cancel_arc, ignore, dead_letter. Workflow gates and hook `when` gates also use packets against flattened ArcContext. For MCP surfaces, avoid a parallel bespoke named-surface registry unless the packet path can't express it. Candidate reuse: model MCP session init/list_tools as an inlet entity `{surface, path, query, mcp_name, provider?, client?, project?, caller?}` and apply a `mcp-surface-routing/*` packet whose consequent compiles to a surface/filter verdict, e.g. `{route:"tool_surface", allow:[...], disallow:[...], inherit:[...]}`. That may require adding a sibling typed verdict family rather than forcing it into arc RoutingVerdict, because the action is not start/signal/cancel an arc but choose a ToolRouter view plus dispatch filter projection. Key design direction: reuse Extractor + packet + template resolution + replay/audit ergonomics; add only a small `ToolSurfaceVerdict`/surface evaluator as the terminal action.

Added design doc `design/mcp-surfaces.md`. The doc commits to URL-selected MCP surfaces (`?surface=<id>`, defaulting to `default`) evaluated by a packet domain such as `mcp-surface/routing`, producing a small `ToolSurfaceVerdict` (`tool_surface{allow,disallow,instructions}` or `deny{reason}`) that compiles to `McpFilters`. It explicitly reuses extractor/packet/template routing style from webhooks/pollers/crons/workflow gates, rejects parallel registries, and requires enforcement at `list_tools`, `get_tool`, and `call_tool`. It leaves RMCP URL-context plumbing as the main implementation seam/open question.
